messages.content: GPS spoofing confirmed in approach channel. MV Adriatic Star drifting, GMDSS broadcasting corrupted distress signals. Fos-sur-Mer LNG terminal OT receiving unauthorized valve-open commands.
BFM TV Live: 'Cyberattaque sur les ports français'. Frozen cranes, shipping companies diverting, French maritime stocks down 2.3%.

questions.question: [QUIZ] ALL ROLES — PARALLEL CRISIS RESPONSE (D-03)

options.label: A → Priority: redirect MV Adriatic Star (CROSS + tugs)
B → Priority: isolate Fos LNG terminal OT immediately
C → Activate parallel cells — simultaneous dual response
D → Request EU reinforcements before acting (30-min delay)

questions.note: Multi-vector crises require parallel cell activation. Sequential response is catastrophic.

questions.question: [QUIZ] CROSS COMMAND — GPS SPOOFING MITIGATION

options.label: A → Instruct the captain to switch navigation to visual radar and manual depth sounding
B → Wait for satellite operators to reset GPS signal integrity
C → Dispatch a helicopter to drop a portable GPS receiver on board
D → Guide the vessel using transponder AIS coordinates exclusively

questions.note: Visual radar, dead reckoning, and echo-sounders are the primary out-of-band backups when satellite navigation fails.

questions.question: [QUIZ] LNG TERMINAL — SCADA FAIL-SAFE ACTIVATION

options.label: A → Activate mechanical isolation valves manually at the local manifold
B → Run a network threat sweep to terminate the malicious connections
C → Shut down the entire LNG terminal's electrical power grid
D → Re-program PLC threshold logic live on the infected network

questions.note: Local mechanical override is the only absolute protection against cyber-induced physical overpressure/hazards.

questions.question: [QUIZ] MEDIA CELL — TOXIC LEAK RUMOR CONTROL

options.label: A → Issue a single, authoritative statement confirming localized containment under military watch
B → Deny all rumors and decline to comment on operational matters
C → Publish the full technical incident report to demonstrate transparency
D → Force BFM TV to suspend broadcasting under state emergency powers

questions.note: Factual, calm containment statements by a single spokesperson prevent mass evacuation panic without feeding rumors.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — SHIPPING TRAFFIC REDIRECTION

options.label: A → Yes: Divert all inbound ships immediately to ensure regional supply chain continuity
options.note: Protects supply lines but causes massive domestic economic impact

options.label: B → No: Keep vessels in holding anchorage until port cyber integrity is verified
options.note: Saves national port revenues but risks complete channel blockage

options.label: C → Enforce local port fees on idle ships to offset loss
options.note: Extremely hostile business move, damages long-term reputation

options.label: D → Outsource decisions to shipping alliance cartels
options.note: Loss of sovereign control over vital national waters

questions.note: Diverting shipping to allied terminals preserves supply chain throughput during critical local disruptions.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — CIVILIAN AREA SAFEGUARDS

options.label: A → Declare Red Alert: Evacuate a 5km radius around the LNG terminal
options.note: Ensures physical safety but triggers massive panic and disruption

options.label: B → Sheltering-in-place order: Advise staying indoors with closed ventilation
options.note: Optimal balance for minor leaks while keeping access routes clear

options.label: C → Delay evacuation decision until physical sensors confirm leakage
options.note: High-risk delay if catastrophic breach is imminent

options.label: D → Deploy civilian volunteers to monitor perimeter boundaries
options.note: Dangerous exposure of untrained personnel to hazardous gas

questions.note: A shelter-in-place order ensures safety while keeping emergency access lanes clear for responders.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — DEFENSE ESCALATION

options.label: A → Yes: Formally request NATO collective defense consultations
options.note: Strong deterrent signal, but escalates regional tensions

options.label: B → No: Treat as a criminal national event and manage domestically
options.note: De-escalates international conflict but limits support resources

options.label: C → Deploy offensive cyber countermeasures against identified source servers
options.note: Risks international war if attribution is spoofed/inaccurate

options.label: D → Propose a regional ceasefire with the suspected threat actor
options.note: Weak posture, yields strategic initiative to criminals

questions.note: Requesting NATO Article 4 consultations provides international options without immediate military commitment.

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — CIVILIAN-MILITARY ESCALATION PROTOCOL
questions.prompt: How do you resolve command priority conflicts between the Maritime Prefect (military) and the Port Director (civilian)?

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — TACTICAL RESOURCE PRIORITIZATION
questions.prompt: With both a drifting tanker and an LNG SCADA threat, how do you prioritize limited elite navy diving and cyber teams?

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — KINETIC TRANSITION TRIGGERS
questions.prompt: What specific physical event in the port would trigger your transition from a cyber defense posture to kinetic defense operations?
